MAJOR ARCANA

Justice — Meaning

Major Arcana

  • CategoryMajor Arcana
  • SymbolLibra / Number 11
  • UprightFairness, Checking the facts, Balance
  • ReversedUnfairness, Jumping to conclusions, Avoiding responsibility

A card about checking facts and fairness instead of deciding on feeling alone.

Justice stands for "Fairness, Checking the facts, Balance" when upright, and "Unfairness, Jumping to conclusions, Avoiding responsibility" when reversed. Compare the good points and the hard points of each option under the same conditions. It helps to check whether your reason is one you could explain to yourself and to others.

Reading it in a decision — In a situation where feeling and principle are both involved, like declining a request, read this card as lining up the other person's circumstances and your own by the same standard, and deciding with a reason you could explain to both. Reversed, check whether you are selectively seeing only the facts that suit you.

The decision this speaks to: When you're torn over saying no

SYMBOLS

The symbols in the picture

A woman holds a sword and a set of scales. The scales are a tool for comparing two things. She shows how to think by the same standard, without favoring one side.

FOR YOUR DECISION

Hints for your decision

How to read it when you are deciding

Justice depicts judging fairly, based on facts, with scales and sword in hand. When feelings sway you and you cannot decide, line up each option's merits and demerits, and its effects on the people involved, by the same standard. The sword means the sharpness of decision; the scales, balance. This card also represents cause and effect. Accepting that the present is the result of past choices makes the next judgment a more honest one.

How to face a familiar worry

This card suits situations where you must keep things principled — contracts, negotiations, where responsibility lies. Upright, looking for a line that not only you but everyone involved can accept yields results that last. Reversed, inspect whether bias or concealment has crept into your judgment, and borrow a third party's eyes if needed.

Questions to ask yourself before you decide

Is this choice fair both to you and to the other person? With feelings removed and only facts placed on the scales, which way do they tip? Can you take responsibility for the result yourself? Is it a judgment whose reason you could explain afterward?

"Ease of moving forward" is the strength of the tailwind behind an option if you move on it now — not a judgment of whether things will turn out well or badly.

Now that you have read the meaning, turn to the decision in front of you. Draw a card and lay your two options side by side.
